Public domain: every person whose words are in this text died in 1925 or earlier, so the term has ended under the law of every country, whichever one first published it.

People: Karl Otfried Müller (author, Wikidata Q62113), died 1840; George Cornewall Lewis (translator, Wikidata Q1230681), died 1863; Henry Tufnell (translator, Wikidata Q5729338), died 1854. They are every person Project Gutenberg's catalog lists for the book ("Müller, Karl Otfried, 1797-1840; Lewis, George Cornewall, Sir, 1806-1863 [Translator]; Tufnell, Henry, 1805-1854 [Translator]") and every person the printed edition's opening pages credit; each death year is Wikidata's.

Printed edition: The history and antiquities of the Doric race [microform], London, John Murray, 1839, the Internet Archive scan https://archive.org/details/historyantiquiti00mlle. Three passages of the Gutenberg text have 77%, 88%, 44% of their four-word runs in the scan's text. The scan does not show the credit of Karl Otfried Müller, whom the catalog lists; the passages show the scan holds this text.
